data.title: Other psoralens: trioxsalen & 5-methoxypsoralen (5-MOP)
data.summary: Photoprotective agents · Furocoumarin photosensitisers used with UVA (PUVA)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Photoprotective agents_

**Class:** Furocoumarin photosensitisers used with UVA (PUVA)

## Mechanism of action
- Intercalate DNA; with UVA form monoadducts (and cross-links with 8-MOP/5-MOP) → antiproliferative, immunosuppressive and melanogenic effects
- Trioxsalen (4,5',8-trimethylpsoralen): more melanogenic, less phototoxic orally; very phototoxic topically and in bath PUVA
- 5-MOP (bergapten): less nausea and less phototoxicity than 8-MOP; needs higher dose

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Vitiligo (trioxsalen orally with sunlight — PUVAsol; trioxsalen bath PUVA)
- Psoriasis and other PUVA indications (5-MOP — used in Europe)

## Dose & formulations
- Trioxsalen 0.6 mg/kg orally 2 h before sunlight/UVA (Indian practice; tablets 5 mg)
- 5-MOP 1.2–1.8 mg/kg orally 2 h before UVA
- Bath PUVA: trioxsalen or 8-MOP dissolved in bath water (e.g. 0.5–1 mg/L), UVA immediately after 15 min soak

## Adverse effects
- Phototoxic burns, PUVA itch, nausea (less with 5-MOP and trioxsalen)
- Long-term PUVA risks: SCC, lentigines, photoageing, cataract

## Contraindications
- As for methoxsalen: photosensitive disorders, pregnancy, children <10–12, melanoma/skin cancer history

## Drug interactions
- Other photosensitisers

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- 5-MOP — less nausea, needs 1.2 mg/kg
- Trioxsalen — popular in India for vitiligo (PUVAsol)
- Bath PUVA avoids systemic side effects

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.23; Khopkar (Psoralens, PUVA and phototherapy). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
